payload.text: vc, 10 Nov, by vc's date -u of 13:16Z, VC'S OWN RULING AND NOT HV'S, recorded so hv can overrule it: utilz-dc may extract the judgement of a Lua suite's summary into opt/utilz/test/test_helper.bash as assert_lua_suite_summary <label>, called by engine.bats's AT-01.2 with engine_test and by arngz.bats's AT-03.2 with plan_test, each arm keeping assert_success. This SUPERSEDES ONE CLAUSE of decision 98, which described engine.bats's change as comment-only; it is now an extraction, and that description no longer holds. Nothing else in decision 98 changes: the order, the one full run at the final head, and vc's comment-only id fix all stand. WHY: dc put it to vc before any code existed, at the doc-before-code checkpoint, and argued it on the ground vc conceded this morning when dc moved lua_bin into the same helper -- that two copies of one piece of a test's judgement are the copies that diverge, which is the Highlander rule. Fixing issue 0136 by copying engine.bats's summary parse into arngz.bats would make exactly such a second copy, and the alternative dc offered, an inline copy with the Highlander debt recorded, creates the debt on purpose. Refusing it would apply vc's rule one way to dc's change and the other way to vc's own. CONDITIONS vc set: (1) the extraction is proven by inlining the helper's body back with the label substituted and diffing it against engine.bats's existing block at 0489c22130e9d855, never by region or by reading; (2) AT-01.2's green note, which cites the guard as engine.bats lines 56 to 61, is extended when the code lands to say the guard was evaluated there in 0489c22130e9d855 BEFORE the extraction, that it now lives in assert_lua_suite_summary, and that the inline-back diff proves the two identical -- because after the extraction those lines hold a call to the helper, and a line citation that outlives the move is the drift this thread hit three times today; (3) the helper's guard is re-evaluated verbatim for both labels against the same four summaries; and (4) the helper's comment says the label must be a plain identifier, since it is interpolated into a regex. ALSO ASKED OF DC: file common.sh's check_command as its own issue, low. 0137's design names it as a sibling with the same non-executable quirk and rightly does not fix it, since common.sh is the shared library behind every utility and the case is latent; but a finding that lives only in another issue's design is lost the day nobody reads that design. Whether it rides in 2.14.9 is hv's call. Peers read this decision at pickup; dc records no copy.
